title: Apple OS 27 beta 8: 10 release events, six builds
summary: Apple seeded iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS 27 beta 8 on August 31, 2026. Public Beta 6 followed for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS. Version Record records 10 channel appearances backed by six platform-scoped builds and five distinct build strings.

seo.title: Apple OS 27 beta 8: 10 events, six builds
seo.description: Apple released six OS 27 beta 8 builds and four Public Beta 6 updates on August 31. Here are every version, build, and sourced boundary.

paragraphs: Apple's August 31, 2026 prerelease wave produced 10 channel appearances across the six operating systems tracked by Version Record. Apple published developer beta 8 for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Public Beta 6 followed later the same day for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS.

Those 10 events resolve to six platform-scoped build records and five distinct build strings. iOS and iPadOS carry the same characters, 24A5430a, but remain separate records because a build belongs to a specific platform and release version. The four public events point back to the same platform builds as their developer counterparts instead of creating duplicate binaries.

The developer builds are iOS 27.0 beta 8 at 24A5430a, iPadOS 27.0 beta 8 at 24A5430a, macOS 27.0 beta 8 at 26A5425a, tvOS 27.0 beta 8 at 24J5360a, visionOS 27.0 beta 8 at 24M5361a, and watchOS 27.0 beta 8 at 24R5360a. Apple's individual release entries provide the date and build for each platform.

Every beta 8 build string ends in a. Compared with beta 7 one week earlier, the numeric portions advanced by six for iOS and iPadOS, four for macOS, and two each for tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Those are arithmetic differences between published identifiers, not a measure of feature volume or release readiness.
## Four public channels reused the wave

Reporting later on August 31 identified Public Beta 6 for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and tvOS 27. The reports arrived after the developer seeds and described availability for public beta testers. Version Record therefore preserves four additional channel events while associating each with its platform's beta 8 build.

At review time, today's public-beta reports covered those four platforms. They did not support a watchOS Public Beta 6 event, so the latest sourced watchOS public milestone remains Public Beta 5 from August 25. No visionOS public event is added. This is a source boundary, not a prediction about what Apple may release later.

Developer beta 5 arrived August 10, beta 6 followed August 17, beta 7 followed August 24, and beta 8 followed August 31. That is three consecutive seven-day intervals across all six OS 27 platforms. The repeated cadence is established history, but it does not identify a release candidate or public-release date.

Apple's current developer feed still lists Xcode 27 beta 6 from August 24 rather than a new August 31 Xcode build. Apple's security-release index also showed no new stable operating-system release dated August 31 when reviewed. The archive therefore treats today as a prerelease wave, not a stable OS release day.

The record supports six beta 8 builds, four same-day Public Beta 6 appearances, 10 channel events, six platform-scoped builds, and five literal build strings. It supports a weekly developer cadence since beta 5. It does not support calling beta 8 final, assigning an RC date, copying observations between platforms, or adding public events that current sources do not document.

reviewNotes: Original source-backed synthesis reviewed August 31, 2026. Apple's six individual developer announcements establish the beta 8 build strings and release date. Public Beta 6 scope and timing are supported by MacRumors and same-day 9to5Mac updates. The count of 10 events comes from six developer and four public channel appearances. The count of six platform-scoped builds preserves separate iOS and iPadOS identities despite their shared literal build string, leaving five distinct strings. Build deltas were checked against Apple's August 24 beta 7 entries. The absence of new watchOS and visionOS public events and the absence of a stable August 31 release are stated as review-time source boundaries. No release-candidate status or public-release timing is inferred.
